title: From virtual address to physical memory
sub: Four memory accesses: a TLB hit, a TLB miss, and a page fault.

frames.caption: A process's virtual pages (4 KB each) and where they really live. The page table (middle) is kept by the kernel in RAM; the TLB (right) is a tiny cache of recent translations inside the CPU.
Access 0x1234: page 1, offset 0x234. TLB hit: page 1 → frame 2 in about a cycle. Physical address 0x2234.
Access 0x1ABC: page 1, offset 0xABC. TLB hit: page 1 → frame 2 in about a cycle. Physical address 0x2ABC.
Access 0x3010: page 3, offset 0x010. TLB miss: walk the page table in memory (tens of cycles) and find frame 7. Cache it in the TLB. Physical address 0x7010.
Access 0x4008: page 4, offset 0x008. Not in the TLB, and the page table says the page isn't in RAM: page fault. The CPU traps into the kernel.
The kernel reads page 4 from disk into free frame 3 (about 100 µs on an SSD, 10 ms on a hard disk: millions of cycles), updates the page table and restarts the instruction. Physical address 0x3008.
